the delineation of a critical region for a clinically recognizable syndrome, which will help in the understanding of its pathophysiology and in the development of a diagnostic test for this syndrome.

the delineation of the 9-q34.3 deletion syndrome and the identification of candidate genes for the phenotypes of this syndrome.

a 1-Mbp segment proximal to the 9qter contains the genes responsible for the specific facial features and severe mental retardation of the 9p34.3 terminal deletions.
the 1-Mb region is the critical region of 9q34 deletion syndrome.

a 1-MB segment at distal 2qter is likely to be a critical region for the 9qter syndrome.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the 9q terminal deletion syndrome is a well defined entity that is characterized by a distinctive phenotype and that can be caused by deletion of a small region at the 9 end of the long arm of chromosome 9.
the 9qter region is a complex genomic region with a large number of genes and regulatory sequences.
the deletion syndrome associated with 9q deletion syndrome can be delineated to a 1-Mbp region at 9q34, and this region contains several genes that are likely candidates to cause the phenotype.
